q: Your watcher callback executes a DOM node height query after a state shift, but receives old measurements because the DOM hasn't updated yet. What option fixes this?
options: Change the flush configuration option to post
Switch execution to alternative watchSyncEffect hooks
Force immediate re-evaluation using deep options
explain: Setting flush to post delays the watcher callback execution until after the rendering framework completes its component updates and flushes real DOM adjustments.

q: An engineer initializes an open collection of asynchronous web socket handlers inside a custom search tool that can be closed manually using a single action. What utility manages this cleanup?
explain: An effectScope instance collects reactive side effects like computed properties and watchers created within its scope. Calling scope.stop() dismantles all collected dependencies simultaneously.

q: You are binding a search query state to a network fetch inside a watchEffect and must prevent duplicate overlapping requests from creating race conditions. How do you handle this?
options: Wrap fetch promises within explicit nextTick functions
Utilize the onCleanup callback parameter in watchEffect
Migrate reactive inputs to separate shallowRef wrappers
Configure your watcher instance using flush sync properties
explain: The watchEffect callback provides an onCleanup function argument. It executes right before the watcher re-evaluates or unmounts, letting you cancel active operations like in-flight network requests.

q: You are initializing a third-party charting library inside an onMounted hook and want to store its instance in state while ensuring it is never wrapped in a Proxy layer. What utility applies?
explain: The markRaw utility stamps an object with a permanent flag that prevents it from ever being transformed into a reactive proxy, avoiding performance overhead and third-party reference mutations.

q: You need to create an input text binding ref that applies a custom debounce delay to prevent processing updates until a user stops typing for 300ms. How do you build this low-level primitive?
options: Construct a custom ref using the customRef factory
Throttle state values using explicit watchSyncEffect parameters
Wrap inputs with standard reactive proxy objects
Defer modifications using asynchronous nextTick promises
explain: The customRef factory gives you explicit control over reactivity. It takes a factory function with track and trigger arguments to manually schedule dependency tracking and update notifications.

q: You are creating a highly optimized grid layout component containing thousands of items where rows should skip re-rendering unless their selected state flags shift. What directive applies?
explain: The v-memo directive accepts an array of dependency values. The virtual DOM diffing engine skips re-rendering and diffing the entire template subtree if those dependency values match their previous values.

q: You are configuring a server-side rendered application where an asynchronous fetch request must run exclusively on the server before serializing HTML content. Which hook handles this?
explain: The onServerPrefetch lifecycle hook runs exclusively on the node server during server-side rendering. The framework waits for its returned promise to resolve before serializing the final component HTML markup.

q: Your server-side rendered application logs hydration mismatch warnings on client load because an element outputs a random number generated in template views. How do you fix this?
options: Isolate the non-deterministic layout inside ClientOnly tags
Enforce synchronous render configurations within defineOptions
Wrap data processing functions within watchSyncEffect loops
Isolate property tracking blocks using customRef utilities
explain: Hydration mismatches occur when server-rendered HTML doesn't match client expectations. Wrapping browser-specific or non-deterministic elements inside a ClientOnly container defers rendering until the client script executes.

q: You are designing an optimization strategy for an application landing view to stream rendering chunks to edge workers incrementally using the Web Streams API. What function do you use?
explain: The renderToWebStream function from vue/server-renderer converts an application instance into a readable web stream, allowing edge environments to stream HTML to browsers incrementally.

q: You are embedding a design system component inside an enterprise application and want it to compile into a native standalone Web Component. Which framework function handles this?
explain: The defineCustomElement method converts a standard single file component into a native Web Component class, packaging styles securely within a true Shadow DOM layer.

q: You are writing a low-level telemetry plug-in that needs to generate unique layout IDs by fetching the private numeric component ID from the active lifecycle setup. What tool resolves this?
explain: The getCurrentInstance function exposes internal component instance structures. It serves as an escape hatch for library developers to inspect internal parameters like unique instance IDs during setup execution.

q: You are optimizing a server-side rendered page to defer the client-side hydration of a heavy comments component until it actually enters the user's viewport. What strategy applies?
explain: The hydrateOnVisible strategy enables lazy hydration under defineAsyncComponent. It uses an internal IntersectionObserver to delay client hydration until the component scrolls into view.

q: You are investigating the internal tracking engine of Vue 3 and need to identify the core map structure used to hold dependency keys for reactive proxy objects. What structure is it?
explain: The reactivity layer organizes dependencies inside a global WeakMap called targetMap. It links target reactive objects to their specific property maps and execution effect subscribers.

q: You notice that a watcher callback processing deep array modifications skips executing when individual array indexes are directly overwritten in state. Why does this happen?
options: Overwriting array indexes is not trackable via proxies
The array reference must be watched with deep configuration
Array modifications require tracking via watchSyncEffect
Index adjustments are omitted from the task queue updates
explain: While proxies intercept array index mutations natively, watching a ref array only monitors top-level reference changes unless you explicitly pass the deep option.

q: You want to create a bidirectional mapping interface for an input field component using a custom object getter/setter layout. Which reactivity pattern accommodates this?
options: A custom customRef proxy hook block
A writable computed property with get and set definitions
A reactive proxy structure tracking deep modifications
An asynchronous nextTick promise callback structure
explain: Computed properties can accept an options object containing get and set methods. This lets you intercept write assignments to transform data before updating your state.

q: You are writing a complex compiler integration tool and need to read the explicit bitwise flag assigned by the template compiler to mark dynamic text nodes. What is this marker called?
explain: The compiler embeds explicit numeric integers called Patch Flags directly into virtual nodes. The runtime uses these bitwise markers to skip unchanged static elements during patch operations.

q: You want to declare a secure global type extension for route meta parameters across your codebase. How do you declare this using TypeScript?
options: Export custom route interfaces using defineOptions declarations
Augment the RouteMeta interface inside the vue-router module
Cast parameters using explicit computed types within components
Extend your properties directly inside generic defineProps calls
explain: You can extend router types by augmenting the RouteMeta interface within the vue-router module declaration. This ensures full type checking for meta parameters across your app.

q: You are developing a dynamic template structure where style rules use hashed class names generated at compile time instead of data attribute styling scope flags. What attribute should you use?
explain: The module attribute activates CSS Modules within single file components. It compiles internal classes into dynamic, hashed class name strings exposed via the reactive $style object.

q: You want to design a robust global application logger that intercept and processes errors specifically captured inside child layout lifecycles. Which configuration hook manages this?
explain: The app.config.errorHandler hook captures unhandled application errors globally. It receives the error instance, the component reference, and location details for monitoring.

q: You notice brief flashes of loading spinners when fast-loading asynchronous components render in your application. What property on defineAsyncComponent addresses this?
explain: The delay option configuration inside defineAsyncComponent sets a grace period threshold. The loading component is skipped if your network loader resolves within that timeframe, preventing layout flickering.

q: You are developing an intricate list component where elements are rearranged, added, and deleted dynamically. What class modifier helps animate these item repositioning movements?
explain: The TransitionGroup tag automatically applies the v-move class during list reorder operations. It uses FLIP animation techniques to calculate position shifts and smoothly slide items.

q: You are managing a highly complex rendering pipeline containing deeply nested loops and want to manually track dependency collection steps during code execution. What hook gives you this visibility?
explain: The onRenderTracked debugging hook fires when a component render function accesses a reactive dependency. This lets you inspect exactly which state keys are being tracked for layout updates.

q: You are profiling a performance issue where multiple synchronous state changes cause consecutive component re-render operations. What mechanism prevents this?
options: The reactivity proxy layer intercepts setter execution loops
The internal scheduler queues and deduplicates jobs in a microtask
The compiler hoists static structures outside render functions
The virtual DOM patch flag framework separates static text nodes
explain: The framework scheduler queues component render jobs inside a microtask pipeline. It deduplicates multiple identical job entries, ensuring your components re-render only once per event loop cycle.

q: You want to create an explicit template ref binding using the modern Vue 3.5 API that eliminates implicit name-matching vulnerabilities. What utility should you declare?
explain: The useTemplateRef utility accepts a clear string argument to target elements. This creates a strongly-typed reference that decouples the javascript variable name from the template attribute string.

q: You want to prevent child updates from propagating up to parent layouts when structural parameters are modified. Which reactive utility extracts a non-reactive reference copy?
explain: The toRaw utility unwraps a reactive proxy to return its underlying plain javascript object, providing a raw reference copy that completely unhooks dependency tracking loops.
